name: Cynthia Lummis
residence: Cheyenne, Laramie County (born in Cheyenne; Congressional Directory)
occupation: U.S. Senator; attorney and rancher (Congressional Directory)
education: B.S., animal science, University of Wyoming, 1976; B.S., biology, University of Wyoming, 1978; J.D., University of Wyoming, 1985 (Congressional Directory for the 117th Congress)
prior_offices: Wyoming House of Representatives, 1979–1982 and 1985–1993; Wyoming Senate, 1993–1994; law clerk, Wyoming Supreme Court, 1985; general counsel, Office of the Governor, 1995–1997; Interim Director of State Lands, 1997–1998; Wyoming State Treasurer, 1998–2006; U.S. Representative, 2009–2017 (Congressional Directory; official Senate biography)
background: Cynthia M. Lummis was born in Cheyenne on Sept. 10, 1954 (Congressional Directory for the 117th Congress). Her official Senate biography says she was born on a cattle ranch in Laramie County and is a three-time graduate of the University of Wyoming in animal science, biology, and law.

The Congressional Directory records her as an attorney (from 1986) and rancher (from 1976); a clerk of the Wyoming Supreme Court in 1985; a member of the Wyoming House of Representatives, 1979–1982 and 1985–1993; a member of the Wyoming Senate, 1993–1994; general counsel in the Office of the Governor, 1995–1997; Interim Director of State Lands, 1997–1998; and Wyoming State Treasurer, 1998–2006. The official State Officers Roster lists Cynthia M. Lummis as Treasurer in the 1999 and 2003 state-officer listings.

She was elected to the U.S. House of Representatives on Nov. 4, 2008, and reelected to the three succeeding Congresses, serving in the 111th through 114th Congresses (Congressional Directory; Congress.gov). Her official Senate biography states that after leaving the House in 2016 she operated her family's cattle ranches and the Sweetgrass development in Laramie County with her brother and sister.

She was elected to the U.S. Senate on Nov. 3, 2020, and was sworn in on Jan. 3, 2021. Her official Senate biography states that she is the first woman to serve as a United States Senator from Wyoming. Official Wyoming Secretary of State general results for Nov. 3, 2020, record 198,100 votes for Lummis (Republican) and 72,766 for Merav Ben-David (Democratic). Her Senate term ends in January 2027, when official-elect Harriet Hageman takes office (WyoVote official list, as of the Nov. 18, 2026 county-officials extract).
